findings.title: Notes: server-side shell
findings.summary: Off (SB_SHELL_BACKEND=off); the front refuses /notes/.shell as well; the add-on is running.

findings.title: Notes: HTTP proxy to the hub's loopback API
findings.summary: SilverBullet has no IP networking, and the web server refuses /notes/.proxy.

findings.title: Notes: no login
findings.summary: Anyone who can open the hub can read and change the notes, and notes can carry scripts (Space Lua, widgets) that run in each reader's browser (on the notes' own address, apart from /admin).
findings.fix: Choose who may open Notes (Apps): users with an account, or you alone; or leave it open if the notes are meant for everyone.

findings.title: The network floor
findings.summary: The hotspot is up and no floor is loaded: a guest on the hotspot reaches every listener on the box (SSH, Syncthing, MQTT, Tailscale, the rest).
findings.fix: Security → What a guest on the hotspot can reach: switch the floor on.

findings.title: Kept-alive connections to the hub
findings.summary: nginx keeps connections open (keepalive 8) and the hub drains request bodies.

findings.title: Request size limit
findings.summary: 1m server-wide.

findings.summary: Set to the connecting address only.

findings.title: A Content-Security-Policy on the hub's origin

steps.title: Unit sandboxing and the build unit

findings.title: Root units with a sandbox line missing
findings.summary: irate-box-ap-dns (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-ap (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-control (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-crashwatch (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-firewall (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-secdoctor (missing ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-tailscale-boot (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-tailscale (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-uplink (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-visitors-switch (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), mosquitto (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), ttyd (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible): a flaw in a root unit is root with nothing in between, and each line missing is one more thing the flaw can reach.
findings.fix: ProtectSystem=strict with real ReadWritePaths, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible; narrow CapabilityBoundingSet and SystemCallFilter where possible.

findings.title: Guest-reachable units with a bare sandbox
findings.summary: irate-box-ci (keeps capabilities: cap_chown cap_dac_override cap_dac_read_search cap_fowner ca): guest-reachable services (the hub, fcgiwrap with cgit and git-http-backend, add-ons) with few of ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc. The git servers run as the same user as the hub, with write access to the root helper's request queue.
findings.fix: Harden the units and give the git servers a user of their own.

findings.title: Builds can reach the hub on loopback (not /admin)
findings.summary: irate-box-ci.service can connect to 127.0.0.1, so builds reach the hub's guest API, as any guest can; /admin refuses them (it needs the front's secret, which builds cannot read).
findings.fix: IPAddressDeny=localhost on the unit, to keep builds off loopback altogether.

findings.summary: running, as hub; no problem found by the generic checks.

findings.title: Syncthing
findings.summary: running, as hub; no problem found by the generic checks or its own probe.

findings.title: MQTT broker for Meshtastic
findings.summary: running, as mosquitto. Port 1883 answers on *, 0.0.0.0, not only on loopback: anyone on the network reaches it directly, not through the front's login. Its install consent says: "The broker answers anyone on the box's network on port 1883, with no login (limited to msh/#). Add it?". Anonymous clients are allowed, limited by the ACL to msh/#.
findings.fix: bind to 127.0.0.1 and route it through the front, unless the network-facing port is the point; an access point's address only, and a password file, once the box is an AP

findings.fix: Keep each only as long as it is needed: rm /etc/sudoers.d/<file>, then check `sudo -n true` fails.

steps.title: The hub's own accounts and sign-in

findings.title: Password hashes
findings.summary: Every account's hash is scrypt, at today's strength.

findings.title: Repository keys trusted for every repository
findings.summary: Keys in trusted.gpg.d (home_mPWRD_OS.gpg, network_Meshtastic_beta.gpg, network_Meshtastic_daily.gpg) can sign packages for any repository, Debian's included. Sources with no Signed-By of their own: home:mPWRD:OS.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/home:/mPWRD:/OS/Debian_13/, network:Meshtastic:beta.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/beta/Debian_13/, network:Meshtastic:daily.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/daily/Debian_13/.
findings.fix: Move each key to /usr/share/keyrings and name it in its source's Signed-By (or [signed-by=…]); then the key vouches for that repository alone.

findings.title: A daily or nightly package channel
findings.summary: network:Meshtastic:daily.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/daily/Debian_13/ /: whatever its project built last lands on this box at the next upgrade, untested.
findings.fix: A release channel (stable or beta), unless the daily one is the point.

findings.title: A vendor kernel
findings.summary: 6.1.115-vendor-rockchip, built 2026-Jul-15: Debian's security tracker does not cover it, so debsecan's view of the box is blind to the kernel, and its fixes arrive only with a new image or kernel package from its maker.
findings.fix: Keep the kernel package current from its maker's repository when online (apt list --upgradable | grep linux-image).

findings.title: Bluetooth is on
findings.summary: bluetoothd runs, with a radio the hub does not use: a listener and a stack of its own, reachable by anyone in range.
findings.fix: systemctl disable --now bluetooth.service (and rtk-bluetooth.service where there is one); enable --now puts it back.

findings.title: Access-point profiles not the hub's
findings.summary: Hotspot (encrypted) in NetworkManager's connections: an access point the image set up, which could come up beside or instead of the hub's.
findings.fix: Delete each that is not yours (the hub's hotspot is not among them).

findings.title: Link protections
findings.summary: protected_symlinks and protected_hardlinks are on.
findings.fix: They only cover sticky world-writable folders: root's writes in hub-owned folders (F3) are not helped.

findings.title: Kernel addresses and log readable by everyone
findings.summary: kptr_restrict=0, dmesg_restrict=0.
findings.fix: sysctl -w kernel.kptr_restrict=1 kernel.dmesg_restrict=1

findings.title: Process hardening (NX, address randomisation, core dumps) (CIS 1.6)
findings.summary: Memory protections that make an exploit harder to aim, and no core dumps from privileged programs. Not met here: enable nx support. (deep audit of 2026-10-12 01:43)
findings.fix: Address randomisation and core dumps are kernel settings (sysctl); NX is the CPU's, reported oddly by the 32-bit ARM kernel.

findings.title: Time synchronisation (CIS 2.2)
findings.summary: A time service (systemd-timesyncd or chrony) keeping the clock right. Not met here: configure systemd-timesyncd, configure ntp. (deep audit of 2026-10-12 01:43)

findings.title: IPv6 (CIS 3.1)
findings.summary: The benchmark turns IPv6 off where it is not used. Not met here: disable ipv6. (deep audit of 2026-10-12 01:43)
findings.fix: Your network may use it; the doctor's "Reached from the internet" step checks what IPv6 exposes.

findings.title: Sending ICMP redirects (CIS 3.2)
findings.summary: A host that is not a router should not tell others how to route. Not met here: disable send packet redirects. (deep audit of 2026-10-12 01:43)
findings.fix: sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0 (and .default): safe on the box, guests' internet included.

checks.what: Disable send packet redirects to prevent malicious ICMP corruption.

findings.title: Network parameters (source routing, redirects, martians, router adverts) (CIS 3.3)
findings.summary: Kernel network settings that refuse forged routes and log impossible addresses. Not met here: disable icmp redirect, disable secure icmp redirect, log martian packets, enable source route validation, disable ipv6 router advertisement. (deep audit of 2026-10-12 01:43)
findings.fix: Mostly safe to set by sysctl; leave accept_ra on if your network gives IPv6 addresses by router adverts.

checks.what: Disable ICMP redirect acceptance to prevent routing table corruption.

Log suspicious packets, like spoofed packets.
Enable RFC-recommended source route validation.
Disable IPv6 router advertisements.

findings.title: Logs live in RAM
